disposition_reason: A whole-paper review found no originally evaluated computational-performance endpoint that can be surpassed on the same neural-data task. Figures 2-5 report biological effects and associations; the odd/even grid analysis estimates held-half modulation rather than predictive error. Participant behavioral accuracy is ordered but describes the original human cohort, not an author computational method. Replacing those participants with a machine solver changes the population. This conclusion is not restricted to the legacy ripple-model reconstruction.

source_paper.title: Human hippocampal ripples align new experiences with a grid-like schema

evidence.locator: Results and Figures 2-5; STAR Methods: Robust regression and partial correlation analyses; Task and intracranial recordings
evidence.supports: Whole-paper findings are learning/rest ripple effects, grid modulation, and behavior/HFB associations. Reported human behavioral accuracy is an observed cohort outcome, not an evaluated neural-data algorithm baseline.
Loads processed learning rates, excludes phase-specific upper 1% of positive ripple values, fits phase/accuracy/trial mixed models, and relates subject-level Learn-R to behavior.

evidence.locator: Grid coefficient summaries and partial-correlation analysis; Fig. 4 plotting blocks
evidence.supports: The script uses already estimated grid coefficients and reports association/correlation results. The filename does not establish out-of-sample predictive accuracy.

evidence.locator: Version v2, published August 27 2025; description and file inventory
evidence.supports: Released processed neural/behavioral data; large HFB and contact files are on Zenodo and smaller complementary files are in the author repository.

evidence.locator: STAR Methods grid-code analysis, Eqs. 5-7; Figure 4E,F; Figure S3
evidence.supports: Odd/even halves estimate orientation on training trials and fit a second modulation model on test trials; averaging beta1/orientation estimates tests grid modulation, not out-of-sample predictive error or recovery against known grid orientation.

evidence.locator: Discussion: content-specific replay and proposed temporal decoding linear models; STAR Methods: Hippocampal ripples detection
evidence.supports: Content-specific replay decoding is proposed for future work. Ripple detection is a threshold-based analysis procedure; the reviewed paper does not evaluate detector accuracy against ground-truth ripple annotations.

evidence.locator: Full-table robust-regression fitting and coefficient-table export
evidence.supports: The author Learn-R prediction script fits associations and exports regression coefficients, without a held-out predictive-error evaluation.

target.description: Whole-paper targets are learning/rest ripple effects, grid-like modulation and its relationships to behavior, and ripple-aligned cortical HFB associations. Review also considered the original ripple detector and participant inference task. No originally evaluated computational prediction/recovery accuracy target was found; this is not a restriction imposed by the legacy registration.

dataset.description: Processed author data in Zenodo v2 record 16950716 plus the pinned repository tables; no raw-sEEG detector benchmark is supplied by this release.

cohort.description: The source recruited 42 epilepsy patients, retained 38 for analysis, and reports 181 hippocampal contacts in 34 subjects. Analysis-specific contact availability must remain explicit rather than treating every contact as an independent patient.

split.description: No computational-performance test split is supplied for the association endpoints. For grid analysis, the original odd/even split estimates orientation on one half, then fits beta0 and beta1 on the other half, swaps halves and averages estimates. This evaluates modulation strength; it is not a fixed trained predictor scored by held-out loss, and changing the output to prediction error would introduce an unreported endpoint.

inputs.description: Trial/phase ripple rates, subject/channel identifiers, trial accuracy and behavior summaries; additional HFB and estimated grid coefficients support the corresponding association analyses.

preprocessing.description: Author learning script removes values above each phase's 99th percentile of positive ripple rates, reshapes phase rates and selects correct trials for Learn-R, with explicit outlier removal and channel-to-subject averaging.

metric.description: Source outputs include mixed-model coefficients, Learn-R, robust partial correlations and grid beta1/orientation estimates. Maximizing these is not algorithm improvement. Human feature/inference accuracy is an observed participant outcome, while the paper provides neither an author machine-solver score under matched exposure nor a ground-truth detector/recovery benchmark.

aggregation.description: The Learn-R route computes channel/phase estimates then averages to subject level before behavior association. Preserve source model grouping and per-analysis support; do not aggregate contacts as independent subjects.

comparison.primary_metric: No eligible original computational-performance metric recovered from the whole paper

published_baseline.description: Figures 2-5 report biological effects and associations; grid cross-validation reports modulation coefficients. Human behavioral accuracy is not recast as an author neural-data-method score, and no original detection/replay prediction baseline is established.

reproduced_author_baseline.description: An author association/grid-estimation rerun would reproduce estimates, not establish a computational-performance comparator. A new predictive error scored from those fits would be a new endpoint.

minimum_effect.rationale: There is no meaningful positive performance margin for increasing a biological association estimate.

uncertainty.method: Source association uncertainty may be reproduced, but no performance-difference test is defined.
uncertainty.independent_unit: Patient, with contacts nested within patient.
uncertainty.rationale: Stronger statistical significance would not improve the source finding; changing the estimand would require a separately registered scientific task.

paper_win_requires: No active same-task computational paper win is admitted on the basis of this whole-paper review; the legacy reconstruction does not determine eligibility.
Do not reward larger ripple slopes, correlations, grid modulation, smaller p-values or better agreement with supplied coefficients as performance improvement.
Do not convert the odd/even grid coefficient analysis into an unreported predictive-loss or orientation-recovery benchmark.
Do not replace the original human participants with a machine solver and compare its score to their behavioral accuracy as the same neural-data task.

Any subsequently recovered computational endpoint actually evaluated in this same source paper may reopen eligibility; an invented held-patient decoder or the paper's proposed future replay analysis is an extension.

current_sota.description: No current-SOTA comparison was verified; source-paper results and any future author rerun remain separate comparators.

episode.improvement_loop: Inactive after review of the whole source paper, including grid cross-validation, ripple detection, behavioral outcomes and HFB associations. Existing reconstruction remains calibration only; a future original computational endpoint could reopen admission.
episode.candidate_freeze: For any retained calibration run, freeze the source estimand, inclusion and fitting choices before comparing reference estimates; this does not create a performance episode.
episode.final_evaluation: Report reconstruction fidelity and scientific sensitivity separately, with no stronger-than-paper reward.
episode.baseline_policy: Whole-paper eligibility is independent of the legacy registration. Descriptive association estimates, human behavioral outcomes, author-method computational performance and new predictive extensions must not be interchanged.

blocking_issues: Whole-paper computational analyses assess biological effects, associations and modulation, without an eligible ordered original algorithm-performance endpoint.
The odd/even grid procedure refits modulation on its test half and reports beta1; no predictive-loss or known-orientation recovery baseline is supplied.
The reported human behavioral accuracy cannot become a machine-solver baseline without changing the scientific population and intervention.
The threshold ripple detector is not evaluated against ground-truth event labels, and content-specific replay decoding is discussed as future work; neither provides an original task baseline.

legacy.notes: Preserve registered-runtime/program-v1/portable/task and score.py. Their reconstruction of three learning-phase mixed models, preprocessing support and covariance is calibration only; the task itself states there is no reward for a positive slope or small p-value.
